basis: Dissection directly damages cervical arterial walls; associated cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication.
Benign neoplasm arising in lung parenchyma or bronchi.
Melanoma originates in the uvea; metastatic disease is not intrinsic involvement of another axis.
Organ-specific hereditary gastric cancer syndrome; breast has no axis. Predisposition alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Neoplasm of the maxillary sinus, an upper respiratory site; jaw involvement and lymphoma are not universal across this umbrella.
Usually an apical lung tumour with defining brachial plexopathy; bony thoracic invasion is usual over its course (>30%). Vascular damage is less consistent.
Structural myopathy with muscle atrophy in 4/4; global developmental delay in 1/2 supports neurologic involvement. Dysphagia alone does not establish GI injury.
Marrow failure and diagnostic nail/skin/oral changes; cirrhosis in 1/2. Intellectual disability in 1/2 omitted at the four-axis cap.
Purely psychiatric delusional disorder without established damage to an organ axis.
Abnormal function of the bladder-ureter junction; the renal axis includes bladder and ureters.
Hirschsprung disease, nail hypoplasia and distal limb hypoplasia define the syndrome. Hydronephrosis is reported without an established common frequency.
Early-onset lamellar lens opacity; broader CRYAB spectrum ancestry does not establish myopathy or cardiomyopathy in this cataract subtype.
Meningeal tumour; chordoid histology does not indicate a skeletal tumour origin.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder of hepatocerebral type; liver failure in 19/19 and characteristic encephalopathy/cerebral injury.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%, supporting pulmonary functional impairment. Developmental delay occurs in only 5-29%.
Isolated congenital cerebellar/posterior fossa malformation; absence of hydrocephalus does not change the neurologic location.
GRIN2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 7/7. Thyroid, airway and skeletal findings are each reported in only 1/6.
Viral or bacterial infection of the tonsils in the pharyngeal upper respiratory tract.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal disease are major BBS criteria; renal insufficiency 1/3. Developmental delay 2/2 and ID 2/4; limb anomalies omitted at cap.
Lens opacity caused by hypocalcemia; the underlying calcium disorder is a cause, not an additional organ damaged by the cataract.
Autoimmune erosive synovitis defines RA. Clinically significant lung disease, vasculitis and other extra-articular damage are minority or separately coded conditions.
Deposits beneath retinal pigment epithelium define an ocular condition; no other organ involvement is established.
Most human poisonings follow ingestion, causing direct GI mucosal injury. Pulmonary and skin injury depend on uncommon exposure routes; systemic failure is variable.
Mature T-cell lymphoma is a haematologic malignancy and qualifies for the lymphoma mechanism axis; common extranodal damage is not established.
Meningeal tumour with microcystic histology; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to this subtype.
